idea: Design quality advisory to real estate funds
buyer: Real estate fund managers buying or developing schemes
pain: Investment teams cannot judge whether a scheme is well designed, which drives long-run value
v1: An independent design assessment of one scheme under offer
verdict: The purest expression of her two careers, but the buyer must first believe design quality is investable.

why.distribution: Warm real estate fund contacts, reachable directly.
why.demand: Inferred entirely from her own conviction; no fund currently pays anyone to assess design quality.
why.fmf: Nobody else can credibly claim both a masters in architecture and eight years of institutional analysis.
why.revenue_structure: Deal by deal, tied to transaction flow.
why.defensibility: Genuinely hard to copy - the combination barely exists in the market.
why.leverage: Each assessment requires her eye on the specific scheme.
why.tailwind: Flat; design quality is not currently a budgeted line in underwriting.
why.ceiling: £6k x 33 schemes = £198k, requiring a volume of deal flow and a habit that does not exist.

ceiling_arithmetic: £6k x 33 schemes = £198k, which needs funds to routinely commission design assessment - a behaviour nobody currently has. Realistic: 5-8 = £30-48k.
carries: The single most defensible founder-market fit in the set. Almost literally nobody else can offer this.
kills: Demand at 2. The pain is hers, not theirs. Funds do not yet believe design quality is an underwritable variable.
test: Offer two real estate PMs a free design assessment on a scheme under offer.
test_pass: One says it changed their price or their mind.
test_fail: They find it interesting but not decision-relevant.
